questions.q: A data lake team wants to detect unusual activity such as bursts of DeleteObject calls and access from malicious IPs on its S3 buckets. Which feature fits best?

options.why: Wrong: Inspector finds software vulnerabilities, not S3 activity threats.
Right: it analyzes S3 data events with threat intelligence and anomaly detection.
Wrong: Macie classifies sensitive data in objects, it does not detect destructive activity patterns.
Wrong: Config checks configuration compliance, not API behavior.

questions.explain: S3 Protection analyzes S3 data events for exfiltration and destructive actions.
questions.remember: Threat or anomalous activity on S3 → GuardDuty S3 Protection.
variants: Where is PII in S3 → Macie.
Vulnerable packages on hosts → Inspector.
Bucket config compliance → Config or Security Hub controls.

questions.q: A security team must find which S3 buckets hold personally identifiable information. Which service should it use?

options.why: Wrong: it detects threats from logs, it does not classify object content.
Wrong: it scans for CVEs and exposure, not data content.
Right: only Macie classifies S3 content for sensitive data.
Wrong: it investigates findings, it does not scan data.

questions.explain: Sensitive data discovery is Macie's job.
questions.remember: Sensitive data in S3 → Macie, not GuardDuty or Inspector.
variants: Threats → GuardDuty.
Vulnerabilities → Inspector.
Investigation of a finding → Detective.

questions.q: A company wants GuardDuty to analyze VPC Flow Logs and DNS query logs. What must the team do to enable these data sources?

options.t: Turn on VPC Flow Logs and Route 53 query logging and send them to S3
options.why: Wrong: GuardDuty does not use your copies of these logs.

options.t: Install the GuardDuty agent on every EC2 instance
options.why: Wrong: the agent is only for Runtime Monitoring, not foundational detection.
Right: it reads CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs internally.

options.t: Create a CloudTrail data event trail
options.why: Wrong: data events matter for S3 Protection, not for flow or DNS sources.

questions.explain: Foundational sources are read internally and are agentless.
questions.remember: GuardDuty foundational detection = one click; no log setup, no agent.
variants: Container or instance OS events → Runtime Monitoring needs an agent.
S3 data event analysis → enable S3 Protection.
Longer finding history → export to S3.

questions.q: GuardDuty reports that an IAM role's temporary credentials are used from an unusual external IP. The company wants automated response. Which design is best?

options.t: EventBridge rule on the GuardDuty finding invoking Lambda to revoke the role session
options.why: Right: findings go to EventBridge in near real time, and revoking the session is preferred over deleting keys.

options.t: Poll the GuardDuty console daily and revoke by hand
options.why: Wrong: slow and manual.

options.t: Add the IP to a GuardDuty trusted IP list
options.why: Wrong: trusted lists suppress findings, which hides the attack.
Wrong: it checks exposure of workloads, not credential misuse.

questions.explain: Detect with GuardDuty, respond via EventBridge and Lambda.
questions.remember: GuardDuty finding → EventBridge → Lambda/Step Functions for remediation; prefer role session revocation over key deletion.
variants: Isolate an EC2 instance → Lambda swaps its security group.
Ticket or alert → EventBridge to SNS.
Known-good IP noise → trusted IP list or suppression rule.

questions.q: A compliance rule requires GuardDuty findings to be kept for 12 months. What should the team do?

options.t: Nothing, GuardDuty keeps findings for a year
options.why: Wrong: GuardDuty keeps findings only 90 days.

options.t: Export findings to S3 encrypted with KMS
options.why: Right: S3 export is needed for retention beyond 90 days.

options.t: Raise a retention setting in the console
options.why: Wrong: the 90-day retention is fixed.
Wrong: Detective investigates, it is not a findings archive.

questions.explain: GuardDuty retains findings 90 days; export to S3 for more.
questions.remember: Need more than 90 days of GuardDuty findings → export to S3 (KMS encrypted).
variants: Analytics over findings → Security Lake or Athena on the export.
Security Hub also consolidates findings but retention there is limited.
Need alerts, not retention → EventBridge.

questions.q: Files are uploaded to a landing bucket and must be scanned for malware before analytics jobs read them. The team wants the least operational work. Which option fits?

options.why: Right: it scans new uploads, tags the result on the object, and can trigger quarantine.
Wrong: it scans function code, not uploaded files.
Wrong: Macie finds sensitive data, not malware.
Wrong: it checks configuration controls, not file content.

questions.explain: Malware Protection for S3 scans new objects and tags them with a scan status.
questions.remember: Malware in uploaded S3 files → GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3.
variants: Malware on EBS volumes of EC2 → Malware Protection for EC2.
Scan status ACCESS_DENIED → check KMS or bucket policy.
Sensitive data → Macie.

questions.q: A team wants continuous scanning of EC2 hosts, ECR images and Lambda dependencies for CVEs, with severity adjusted by network exposure. Which service?

options.why: Wrong: it detects threats, not package vulnerabilities.
Wrong: it tracks configuration, not CVEs.
Right: it continuously scans and uses a risk score that adjusts CVSS for the environment.
Wrong: it covers S3 sensitive data.

questions.explain: Inspector is vulnerability management with an environment-adjusted risk score.
questions.remember: Vulnerabilities and CVEs on EC2, ECR, Lambda → Inspector.
variants: Threats → GuardDuty.
Patching the found issues → Systems Manager Patch Manager.
Inspector not scanning EC2 → check SSM Agent and coverage view.

questions.q: Inspector shows no findings for several EC2 instances. Coverage reports them as not scanned. What is the most likely cause?

options.why: Wrong: GuardDuty is independent of Inspector scanning.

options.t: SSM Agent is not running or the instance has no SSM role
options.why: Right: agent-based scanning depends on Systems Manager, and the coverage view shows why.

options.t: The instances have no public IP
options.why: Wrong: scanning does not require a public IP.
Wrong: Security Hub only receives findings, it does not drive scanning.

questions.explain: Missing SSM Agent or role is the classic reason; also unsupported OS.
questions.remember: Inspector not scanning EC2 → check SSM Agent, SSM role, OS support in the coverage view.
variants: ECR not scanned → enhanced scanning not enabled.
Findings missing in Security Hub → integration or Region problem.
Many ECR rescans costing more → review rescan duration.

questions.q: Security Hub controls for a new account show no data and no evaluations. What prerequisite is probably missing?

options.t: AWS Config enabled and recording resources
options.why: Right: most Security Hub controls use Config rules and need recording.
Wrong: GuardDuty is a finding source, not required for control checks.
Wrong: not part of control evaluation.
Wrong: unrelated to controls.

questions.explain: Controls run on AWS Config service-linked rules.
questions.remember: No control results in Security Hub → enable AWS Config and recording in that account and Region.
variants: No GuardDuty findings in Security Hub → integration or Region mismatch.
Global IAM resources → record in one Region only.
Config cost → recording scope matters.

questions.q: A company with 80 accounts in 3 Regions wants one dashboard of GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and compliance findings. Which setup is best?

options.t: Security Hub with a delegated administrator and cross-Region aggregation
options.why: Right: it normalizes findings and consolidates members and linked Regions into one aggregation Region.
Wrong: no consolidation, high effort.
Wrong: it queries API events, it does not normalize security findings.
Wrong: it investigates, it does not aggregate posture.

questions.explain: Security Hub aggregates and normalizes findings across accounts and Regions.
questions.remember: One view over many accounts and services → Security Hub, delegated admin plus aggregation Region.
variants: Auditors want CIS benchmark → enable the CIS standard with Config.
Long-term analytics → Security Lake or Firehose export.
Investigate one finding → Detective.

questions.q: A known and accepted finding keeps appearing in Security Hub and distorts the security score. What is the best fix with little effort?

options.t: Delete the Security Hub service-linked role
options.why: Wrong: this breaks the service.

options.t: Create an automation rule that suppresses matching findings with a note
options.why: Right: automation rules update findings automatically at ingestion.
Wrong: removes the control evaluations for everything.
Wrong: insights only group findings, they do not change them.

questions.explain: Automation rules suppress or change findings by criteria.
questions.remember: Recurring accepted finding → Security Hub automation rule to suppress with a note.
variants: Notify on Critical findings → EventBridge rule.
Manual push of selected findings to a workflow → custom action.
Raise or lower severity automatically → automation rule.

questions.q: A critical Security Hub finding must create a ticket automatically. Which design fits?

options.t: EventBridge rule on Security Hub findings with severity Critical, targeting Lambda or SNS
options.why: Right: Security Hub publishes finding events (source aws.securityhub) to EventBridge.

options.t: CloudWatch metric alarm on finding counts
options.why: Wrong: Security Hub has no native finding metrics.
Wrong: it hides findings, it does not notify.
Wrong: unrelated to security findings.

questions.explain: Findings reach EventBridge, which fans out to Lambda, SNS or ticketing.
questions.remember: Alert or ticket from Security Hub → EventBridge rule on findings.
variants: Rule not firing → check pattern source aws.securityhub and the Region.
Third-party findings in → BatchImportFindings.
Selected findings by analyst click → custom action to EventBridge.
